analysis.title: Snap Inc. (SNAP) Q3'26 Review: Mixed Topline Results Despite Building Momentum Around Key Growth Initiatives & Continued Operating Leverage
key_insights: GS maintains a Neutral rating and a $6.50 12-month price target on SNAP (price $5.92, 9.8% upside) after the Q3'26 report. The target is unchanged.
Q3'26 total revenue was $1,722mm, about in line with guidance ($1.70-1.74bn) and slightly below GS ($1,730mm) and consensus ($1,732mm). Revenue grew 14% YoY and 8% QoQ.

Advertising revenue grew about 4% YoY, below management's ambitions. Upper-funnel brand advertising declined YoY, mainly from weaker CPG spending and macro pressure in the US and Middle East. Progress on new ad formats (Chat/Sponsored Snaps, Promoted Places, Spotlight) only partly offset this.
Other (subscription) revenue grew 84% YoY and is now about 20% of total revenue, driven by roughly 30mm paid subscribers. GS cites strength in Snapchat+, Memories Storage and Lens+.

Adj. EBITDA of $383mm (22.2% margin) beat GS ($338mm) and consensus ($339mm) and the $300-350mm guide. Management said 93% of incremental revenue flowed through to Adj. EBITDA, helped by opex discipline and restructuring savings.
Gross margin was 62.3% against GS at 58.7% and consensus at 59.0%. GAAP EBITDA was $121mm against $63mm for GS and $65mm for consensus.

Total DAUs of 495mm missed GS (501mm) and consensus (499mm). The planned switch to MAU as the primary audience metric in Q1'27 may reinforce investor concerns about moderating user growth, since management prioritizes engagement quality over DAU maximization.
Europe revenue ($363mm) and Rest of World revenue ($345mm) were below GS and consensus, and both regions slowed sequentially in YoY growth. North America revenue ($1,014mm) beat both.

GS raised Q4'26E to revenue of $1.98bn, Adj. EBITDA of $511mm and GAAP EPS of $0.09. FY2027E moves to revenue of $7.58bn, Adj. EBITDA of $1.65bn and GAAP EPS of $0.13. Revenue changes are small, and the EBITDA and EPS increases come from margin.

GS cut DAU forecasts, mostly in Rest of World: FY2027E total DAUs fall 4% to 510mm and FY2028E fall 5% to 522mm. Europe and Rest of World revenue estimates are also reduced, and North America is raised.

Management is optimistic about the long-term shift toward AR/spatial computing, including the recent launch of its SPECS hardware and software development service. GS sees the near-term focus on re-accelerating revenue growth through core ads (direct response, new formats and verticals) and newer monetization such as subscriptions and SPECS.

The price target blends 1.5x EV/Sales on NTM+1 year estimates with a modified DCF at 20.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA on NTM+4 years estimates, discounted back 3 years at 12%. The scenario range is $4.00 downside, $6.50 base and $9.00 upside.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and the $6.50 target after Q3'26. Subscription growth and margin gains are offset by slow ad growth, a DAU miss and weaker Europe and Rest of World revenue.

earnings_insights: SNAP Q3'26 reported revenue was $1,722mm against GS est. $1,730mm, consensus est. $1,732mm and company guide of $1.70-1.74bn. It rose 14% YoY.
SNAP Q3'26 reported Adj. EBITDA was $383mm (22.2% margin) against GS est. $338mm, consensus est. $339mm and guide of $300-350mm.

SNAP Q3'26 reported GAAP EBITDA was $121mm (7.0% margin) against GS est. $63mm and consensus est. $65mm. Reported gross profit was $1,073mm (62.3% margin) against GS est. $1,016mm and consensus est. $1,021mm.
SNAP Q3'26 reported GAAP EPS was $0.03 against GS est. $(0.02) and consensus est. $0.00.
SNAP Q3'26 reported total DAUs were 495mm against GS est. 501mm and consensus est. 499mm. By region: North America 92mm, Europe 98mm, Rest of World 305mm.
SNAP Q3'26 reported regional revenue: North America $1,014mm (above GS est. $999mm), Europe $363mm (below GS est. $369mm) and Rest of World $345mm (below GS est. $362mm).
GS Q4'26E (estimate, raised): revenue $1,979mm (from $1,955mm) against company guide of $1,950-1,985m. Adj. EBITDA is $511mm (from $443mm) against guide of $490-525m. GAAP EPS is $0.09 (from $0.04).
GS FY2026E (estimate): revenue $6,830mm, Adj. EBITDA $1,377mm and GAAP EPS $(0.02), from $(0.12) before.

GS FY2027E (estimate): revenue $7,576mm, Adj. EBITDA $1,651mm (from $1,524mm) and GAAP EPS $0.13 (from $0.05). FY2028E (estimate): revenue $8,279mm (from $8,317mm), Adj. EBITDA $1,893mm and GAAP EPS $0.21 (from $0.15).
Management said Sponsored Snaps grew 56% QoQ and Spotlight average eCPM grew 22% YoY in Q3'26.
risk_factors: Advertiser demand headwinds (platform policy changes, macro conditions, competition) persist longer or recover faster than GS models.
Competition for user growth, engagement and advertising dollars from incumbent and emerging internet, media and commerce companies.
Ability to capitalize on the global user growth opportunity, with DAUs below estimates and Rest of World forecasts cut.
Margin pressure from platform and content initiatives worse than modeled, against upside from ARPU growth and cost-cutting.
Regulatory environment for user data and privacy.
Execution on monetizing growth initiatives (Maps, Games, Minis, AR initiatives with Camera).
Exposure to global macro volatility and investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
geopolitical: Management cited macro pressure in the US and Middle East as a drag on advertising spend in Q3'26.

tension_points.bull_case: New ad formats (Sponsored Snaps +56% QoQ, Spotlight eCPM +22% YoY, Promoted Places) are gaining traction with improving advertiser performance. Direct-response mix and new verticals could offset brand weakness, and subscriptions plus SPECS add newer revenue streams.
tension_points.bear_case: Advertising revenue grew only about 4% YoY. Upper-funnel brand advertising declined on weaker CPG spending and macro pressure in the US and Middle East, and DAUs missed estimates with the MAU metric switch coming in Q1'27.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS says the view changes if current advertiser demand headwinds deviate from its expectations, either persisting longer or recovering faster than modeled.

theme_stances.key_argument: Investor focus stays on re-accelerating total revenue growth from core ads and newer monetization such as subscriptions and SPECS.
theme_stances.evidence: ability to reaccelerate total revenue growth from a mix of core ads

theme_stances.key_argument: Subscription and direct revenue streams continue to scale, led by Snapchat+, Memories Storage and Lens+.
theme_stances.evidence: Subscription and direct revenue streams continue to scale
